standard.title: Footwear for Men and Women for Municipal Scavenging Work — Specification
standard.description: This standard prescribes the requirements, sampling guidelines, and testing methods for protective and occupational footwear used by municipal workers during scavenging and waste handling operations under dry and wet conditions. Because municipal workers frequently work in unhygienic, water-logged areas and come in contact with infectious contaminants, glass shards, or needles, the footwear utilizes non-leather uppers (since leather is highly unsuitable for wet environments). Occupational footwear is specified for light-duty work, whereas protective footwear is designated for environments requiring active impact protection.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Footwear made from All Rubber and all Polymeric Material and its Components (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all footwear for municipal scavenging work manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, importing, or selling non-certified scavenging boots is a statutory offense. Export-only products are exempt if they conform to foreign buyers' specifications. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polymeric/rubber scavenging footwear.
requirements: Every boot conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the size, manufacturer's name/brand, year and month of manufacture, standard reference (IS 16994), and if the boot is protective or occupational.

To prevent premature wear or degradation during physical field work, all markings must be applied on the side of the tongue or at the top outer face of the boot where they suffer the least amount of abrasion.

The footwear is classified into three design varieties depending upon structure and protection level: Type 1 (Class I or II of IS 15298), Type 2 (Class II gumboots of IS 15298), and Type 3 (Class II Wellington/knee boots of IS 15298).
The uppers must be leak-proof, using either a polymeric/elastomeric upper or a vulcanized rubber upper with a textile fabric backing at the reverse side, and must belong to Class I or II of IS 15298.

For protective footwear variants (variety 2 and 3 of scavenging work), an integrated protective toe cap must be built in, satisfying the impact energy and static compression thresholds defined in IS 15298 (Part 3) Clauses 5.3.2.3 and 5.3.2.4.
To prevent water seepage and sole delamination, the joint adhesion strength must be at least 4.0 N/mm. If a material tear occurs during testing, the bond strength must not fall below 3.0 N/mm.

If outsoles or other components are manufactured from Polyurethane (PU), they must undergo hydrothermal aging per Clause 8.5 of IS 15298 (Part 1) and meet the physical thresholds of Clause 5.8.5 of IS 15298 (Part 3/4).

If natural or synthetic rubber is used in construction, the finished whole footwear must be subjected to heat aging at 100 ± 1 °C for 24 hours, and must develop zero physical tackiness or brittleness.

To guarantee user health, materials must remain free from restricted phthalate plasticizers. The prohibited substances include Diisobutyl phthalate (DIBP), Di-Isononyl phthalate (DINP), Di-n-Octyl phthalate (DNOP), Di-Isodecyl phthalate (DIDP), Di-(2-methoxyethyl)-phthalate (DMEP), Di-n-hexyl phthalate (DnHP), and other branched or linear alkyl esters.
The textile backings and lining fabrics must show zero presence of allergenic disperse dyes when analyzed in accordance with the pyridine-water extraction methods of IS 16914 (Part 2).
The tensile strength and extension limits of shoe laces must be verified using a tensile testing machine on conditioned specimens in both dry and wet states.
Manufacturers are required to make a clear statutory declaration on the product labeling regarding whether the footwear materials are biodegradable or non-biodegradable.
